Private Key Header.description: According to NIST SP 800-57 key-management guidance, private keys must be held in protected key storage such as an HSM or KMS. A private key readable from a datastore compromises every system that trusts it.
Private Key Header.remediation_advice: Revoke and reissue the affected key pair, and move private keys to a managed KMS or HSM.
Private Key Header.validation: PEM header/footer framing; base64 body parses as DER.

AWS Secret Access Key.finding_name: AWS secret access key in plain text
AWS Secret Access Key.description: AWS security guidance and the CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark prohibit storing long-term access keys in datastores. A leaked secret key grants full API access as its principal.
AWS Secret Access Key.remediation_advice: Deactivate and rotate the key in IAM, then replace stored long-term credentials with IAM roles or short-lived STS credentials.
AWS Secret Access Key.validation: 40 base64 chars; valid only when paired with a live access key ID.

Password Pattern.description: According to NIST SP 800-63B section 5.1.1.2, passwords must be stored salted and hashed with an approved one-way key-derivation function. Plain-text password storage is never permitted.
Password Pattern.remediation_advice: Force a reset of the affected credentials and store passwords using Argon2, bcrypt, scrypt, or PBKDF2.

AWS Access Key.finding_name: AWS access key ID in plain text
AWS Access Key.description: An access key ID identifies a long-term AWS credential and is almost always stored alongside its secret key. The CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark requires long-term keys to be minimized and rotated.
AWS Access Key.remediation_advice: Audit the key's usage in IAM, rotate it, and prefer IAM roles with temporary credentials.

API Key.description: API keys are authentication credentials; OWASP ASVS secrets-management requirements mandate storage in a dedicated secrets manager, not in application datastores.
API Key.remediation_advice: Rotate the exposed key and move service credentials to a secrets manager with scoped permissions.

Bearer Token.description: Per OAuth 2.0 bearer token usage (RFC 6750), possession of the token alone grants access, so tokens must not be stored where they can be read and replayed.
Bearer Token.remediation_advice: Revoke the affected tokens, shorten token lifetimes, and persist only hashed token references.
mitre_attack: T1550.001 (Use Alternate Authentication Material: Application Access Token)

OAuth Token.description: The OAuth 2.0 Security Best Current Practice requires access and refresh tokens to be protected at rest; refresh tokens in particular grant long-lived account access.
OAuth Token.remediation_advice: Revoke the tokens at the authorization server and encrypt or hash stored token values.
mitre_attack: T1550.001 (Use Alternate Authentication Material: Application Access Token)

compliance_frameworks: GDPR Art. 4(1) (claims may embed personal data)
JWT Token.description: A signed JWT is replayable as a bearer credential until it expires, and its claims frequently embed personal data. Raw JWTs must not persist in readable datastores.
JWT Token.remediation_advice: Invalidate the affected sessions, shorten JWT lifetimes, and avoid persisting raw tokens.
mitre_attack: T1550.001 (Use Alternate Authentication Material: Application Access Token)
JWT Token.validation: Three base64url segments starting eyJ; header and payload decode as JSON; signature verifiable with issuer key.

Secret.ActivationOrAuthKey.description: Session tokens, activation keys, nonces, and salts are authentication material; OWASP session-management guidance requires them to be unpredictable and protected at rest.
Secret.ActivationOrAuthKey.remediation_advice: Invalidate active sessions and activation keys, and store only hashed values.
mitre_attack: T1550.001 (Use Alternate Authentication Material: Application Access Token)

Secret.PasswordHash.description: According to NIST SP 800-63B, password hashes must use a salted, compute-hard function. Readable hashes are subject to offline cracking, and legacy schemes such as MD5-based phpass fall quickly.
Secret.PasswordHash.remediation_advice: Migrate to Argon2, bcrypt, or scrypt, force resets for accounts with weak hashes, and restrict read access to credential columns.
cwe: CWE-916 (Password Hash With Insufficient Computational Effort)
Secret.PasswordHash.validation: Hash-format prefixes: $P$/$H$ phpass, $2y$ bcrypt, $argon2, MD5 hex.

High Entropy Secret.description: A string with the statistical profile of a machine-generated secret was detected outside a secrets manager. Unclassified secrets in datastores defeat rotation and audit controls.
High Entropy Secret.remediation_advice: Identify the secret's type and owner, rotate it, and move it to a secrets manager.
High Entropy Secret.validation: Shannon entropy >= 4.5 over a 24+ char token; slug/hex shapes excluded.

Secret.TokenLikeValue.description: A value shaped like an authentication token was detected without corroborating column context. Treat it as a credential until classified otherwise.
Secret.TokenLikeValue.remediation_advice: Review the column's contents, then either classify the value as non-sensitive or rotate it.
Secret.TokenLikeValue.validation: Value shape heuristic (length + charset); no corroborating column name.
